title: 2k/3 Is pixelorama good for making assets?

posts.author: CT99
posts.body: Hey, I wanna ask a question, can pixelorama be a good program for making assets for rpg maker 2003? I'm trying to make my own for any future games that I wanna make. Also, any good tutorial videos to watch so I can get a better grasp at it. Pls and thanks

posts.author: Akkari
posts.body:
I believe it's alright? I remember taking a small look at it on my Raspberry Pi I think.
I personally use and recommend
Pro Motion NG
which does have a free version you can download and try out.
The Indie Dev Community favourite is
Aseprite
, which you can compile for free, there's also a community fork?(if that's the correct term) of Aseprite that's based on an older version which is free called
Libresprite
My preferred graphics tool if I needed something free, is actually
Graphics Gale
, it was an old favourite in the RPG Maker community I believe, alongside
Idraw3
An alternative free software that I like is
GrafX2
, it's definately not for everyone, it's got a rather dated UI, but that's on purpose, because it's suppose to mimic the famous Deluxe Paint by EA, which was used for many games in the late 80s and 90s(Monkey Island, ID Software's Games including DOOM, Another World, Earthworm Jim etc). Fun fact, Pro Motion NG was also created with Deluxe Paint as an inspiration.
If you plan on uploading anything online, you may want something different that can scale well. For this purpose, I recommend using
Inkscape
for site images etc, but if you want to create more 'concept art' like stuff, then I recommend more raster focused programs(but not with pixel art in mind) like
Gimp
or
Krita
.
So for me, I have Pro Motion NG for game art, Inkscape for itch.io etc(what I call promotional artwork), and Gimp if I want to try my hand at concept art(hardly ever do this because I'm bad at art really lol).
Although, I do have a fourth graphics program, and that's
Wonderdraft
, I use this for designing world and region maps. This isn't needed though, you can do the same thing with Gimp or Inkscape, but I bought this ages ago for my world building, it's essentially a RPG Maker of the map making world.
Anyway, as for tutorials, my best advice is to study the asset standards part of the manual(found under help, or if you go into the RPG Maker 2003 folder where your steam games are located(so where the editor exe is found, not the rpg_rt exe in your project folder), you'll find a rpg2003.chm file, that's the manual.
Then in addition to the manual, I would watch
this video
on Autotiles, just to note though that RPG Maker 2000/2003 is different to what the video shows in that it's 3x3 not 2x2, but the process is pretty much the same. Autotile corners are always half of what the engine's tile size is, the video shows 24x24 as it's a tutorial with RPG Maker MV/MZ in mind, so for 2000/2003 which uses 16x16 it's 8x8. In fact, I kinda recommend to just to treat auto tiles as being built up from 8x8 tiles, rather than 16x16.
Also, the extra tile you get with RPG Maker 2k/2k3's 3x3 Autotiles inbetween the representative pattern and corners is the 'parent pattern', this is like the grass or snow underneath a mountain or forest autotile, you find this information in the manual.
